newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bourse halts Uniceramic pricing.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bourse halts Uniceramic pricing.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange said on Monday it will suspend the pricing of the shares of tiles maker Uniceramic for two days as of Tuesday after the company increased its capital threefold.

"The Beirut bourse committee, in a accordance with articles 144, 145, 146 and 147, decided to suspend the pricing of Uniceramic's three types of shares, A, B and C on November 26 and 27," the bourse said in a circular.
"The shares' pricing will resume on Thursday November 28 on the basis of a special pricing," the bourse said, adding that the circular will be effective until further notice.

Article 144 of the bourse regulations states that special pricing rules apply to shares being re-priced after a suspension or which are being traded for the first time, and article 145 allows the committee to set the maximum price fluctuations.

The bourse said Uniceramic increased its capital in June to 18.14 billion Lebanese pounds from 6.05 billion -- 9.5 billion through an asset re-evaluation and a cash injection of 2.59 billion through issuing 1,296,000 shares of 2,000 pounds each.
Uniceramic's shareholders approved the changes at a meeting on November 4.
Its Bearer C shares, the only ones traded on the bourse since all three types were listed in May, last changed hands at $3.25 on June 14.
The two other types of Uniceramic shares are Nominal A shares reserved for Lebanese and Nominal B for Lebanese and non-Lebanese.
After the capital increase, the company's total 9,072,000 shares were divided equally between the three types.
The only actively traded shares on the bourse are those of Solidere. Also listed are shares of Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs and Eternit.
